summary: Paul W. Kroll is a sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (circa 1967–1976). He served as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chair (~1979–1989) and held another post (~1989) at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Paul Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Sussex and Oxford, he held posts at Wadham College, Oxford (1977–1980), the University of Bristol (circa 1980–2011), and Calgary (1999–2000).

Paul de Lagarde was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg, including under Friedrich Rückert, and held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1851–1854) and Göttingen (~1869–1891).

Paula K. R. Arai specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from Kalamazoo College, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. Her posts include Vanderbilt (1994–2002), LSU (2007), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

Paulinus a Sancto Bartholomaeo was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, Sapienza University of Rome, and Collegio San Pancrazio. He served at the Malabar Mission (1776–1789), Congregation of the Index (1800), and Pontifical Urban University (1800).

Pe Maung Tin was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as professor and principal at Rangoon (1912; 1937–1946) and principal at the University of Adult Education (1947).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She earned a BA from National Taiwan University and a PhD from UCLA (2002), studying under Donald F. McCallum, Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

Peipei Qiu is a scholar of Japanology and sinology. She studied at Peking University and Columbia University under Donald Keene and Paul Rouzer, and held an academic post at Vassar College, attested in 2005.

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist and religious studies figure. Educated at Sarah Lawrence and UC Berkeley, she studied under Chögyam Trungpa and other teachers. She served as director of Boulder Shambhala Center (~1981–1985) and led Gampo Abbey.
Pema Gyaltsen studied under Palden Sherab and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and taught Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Pema Namgyel studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Pema Sherpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Pema Tsewang Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and Patrul Rinpoche. He taught Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Terton Sogyal, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Pema Wangchok Gyelpo (1886–1952) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under masters including Shenphen Nangwa and Mipam Gyatso, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and others.
